card: Updates P2PConnection in the Python test framework to wait for the complete 24-byte v1 header before validating magic bytes, mirroring bitcoind's V1Transport::readHeader. Currently, if socket reads arrive in small chunks, P2PConnection disconnects after 4 bytes on non-matching data before bitcoind sends 24 bytes, preventing bitcoind from triggering its v2-to-v1 fallback and causing p2p_v2_encrypted.py to time out. The failure was demonstrated using a forced-chunking test reproducer in PR #36724.
changed_since_previous: None; the previous description was generated without a patch-id.
evidence: Author demonstrated the failure in PR #36724 with a reproducer that forces socket sends into smaller chunks.
Related tracking issue #36726 documents test fragility caused by socket chunking assumptions.
problem: If network socket data arrives in small chunks, the test framework could reject a connection after seeing only 4 bytes of non-magic data. Because bitcoind's v2 transport only falls back to v1 if at least 24 bytes (a full v1 header) were transmitted prior to disconnection, this premature rejection prevents the v1 fallback and causes p2p_v2_encrypted.py to time out.

risk.why: Touches only functional test framework P2P message parsing logic.

summary: Updates the test framework's P2PConnection v1 message parser to verify network magic bytes only after receiving the full 24-byte header rather than checking after just 4 bytes. This mirrors bitcoind's V1Transport behavior.
